reasoning: Split corn stalk shows tan/straw-colored pith with numerous small black pycnidia (fruiting bodies) dotting the surface and dark necrosis at the node. This pattern — light-colored decaying pith with embedded black pycnidia and dark node browning — is characteristic of Diplodia stalk rot (Stenocarpella maydis). Anthracnose stalk rot was ruled out because it produces shiny black external rind lesions rather than pycnidia on tan interior pith. Charcoal stalk rot was ruled out due to absence of stringy/shredded gray pith with fine sclerotia.
